method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs
why_not_one_block_off: PRINTED NAME: the corridor is lettered AVENUE S down the roadway on BOTH sheets - sheet 89 at native x~2165, sheet 98 at native x~180. AVENUE-FACE RUNS: on 89 its west face carries 4102-4128 and its east face 4101-4127, i.e. the 41st-42nd segment of Ave S; on 98 its east face carries 4201-4227 (42nd-43rd) and 4301-4327 (43rd-44th). CROSS-STREET RUNS (the hundred-block test): on sheet 89 along 42nd St, the seam street, the run west of the line ends 2410 2412 | 2414 2416 2418 2420 2422 2424 and the run east of it begins 2502 2504 2506 - a 2400|2500 transition; the same break repeats on 41st and 40th St (...2421 2423 | 2501 2503 2505). On sheet 98 along 42nd St the run east of the line begins 2501 2503 2505 2507 2509 2511 (2502 2504 2506 on the 43rd St face); the 2400 block west of it lies off-sheet on plate 97. THE 2500 BLOCK CLOSES THE IDENTIFICATION FROM BOTH SIDES: on both plates the 2500 block is bounded by Ave S on the west and Ave S 1/2 on the east - on 89 Ave S 2150.8 -> Ave S 1/2 ~3146 (996 px), on 98 Ave S 186.8 -> Ave S 1/2 1178.6 (992 px) - and on 98 that block's 20-ft mid-block alley measures 683.1, against 682.7 predicted as the midpoint of those two corridors. ONE BLOCK WEST is AVENUE R 1/2 - on 89 at native 1163, where the runs go 2300|2400; it is not on sheet 98 at all. ONE BLOCK EAST is AVENUE S 1/2 - on 89 at ~3146, on 98 at 1178.6 - where the runs go 2500|2600. Neither shows a 2400|2500 break, so neither can be this line. NOTE ON EQUAL-NATIVE-X (rejected): sheet 98's grid sits ~1964 px, i.e. TWO full avenue blocks, WEST of sheet 89's (89: R ~151, R 1/2 1163, S 2150.8, S 1/2 ~3146; 98: S 186.8, S 1/2 1178.6, T 2175.3, T 1/2 ~3165). Matching by near-equal native x would tie Ave S on 89 to Ave T on 98 - two blocks off. The proposed candidates (89: 774 / 1765 / 2757; 98: 768 / 1769 / 2771) pair off almost exactly by native x and are precisely that artefact; none is a corridor.
measurement_note: Native x = raster x of work/sheets/1912w/u<unit>.jpg (3327x3898), origin top-left. Value is the midpoint of the two block-face lines bounding the 70-ft roadway, measured in the block row ADJACENT to the 42nd St seam: sheet 89 the 41st-42nd row (faces 2048.0 / 2253.6 at y=3190, width 205.6), sheet 98 the 42nd-43rd row (faces 83.1 / 290.4 at y=890, width 207.3). Sheet 89 carries a real skew in this row, its corridor drifting ~-0.011 px/row (Ave S centre 2164.0 at y=2100 in the 40th-41st row, 2150.8 at y=3190 in the seam row), so the seam-row value is the one that registers the seam; both faces drift together and the roadway width stays 205-206 px. On sheet 98 the west face at 83.1 sits close to the sheet's west margin, so it was checked two further ways and agrees: east face 290.4 minus half the plate's own roadway (Ave S 1/2 measures 1075.0 / 1282.1 = 207.1 wide) gives 186.9, and the 2500 block's alley centre 683.1 mirrored about Ave S 1/2 (1178.6) gives 187.6. Ave S 1/2 was measured as a parallel control (89 ~3146, 98 1178.6) and implies an inter-sheet offset within ~4 px of the Ave S result; Ave S was reported because both of its faces are drafted block faces on 89 and its width agrees to 1.7 px between plates.
